title: Singapore bars Alice Huang from reentry, says investigation into Megaspeed remains ongoing
snippet: Singapore said it independently investigated Hong Kong resident Alice Huang and Singapore-registered Megaspeed International over suspected false declarations involving servers exported through Singapore, while stressing that companies must consider foreign export controls. The case highlights Singapore's position on cross-border trade, cooperation with overseas authorities, and enforcement against alleged dishonest practices.

title: SK Hynix's HBM4 yield tops 70% as Samsung expands chip packaging capacity

title: Asus sees no major order impact from financing and data-center regulation changes
snippet: Tighter financing and stricter local oversight could lead to consolidation among weaker cloud providers and greater concentration in the data-center industry, Asus said. However, based on its current customer mix and preliminary customer feedback, the company has not seen major effects on construction plans or orders for the fourth quarter of 2026 or 2027.

title: Applied Materials posts record fourth-quarter revenue as AI-driven chip equipment demand accelerates
snippet: Applied Materials' record fourth-quarter revenue and operating income highlight how investment in AI infrastructure is translating into demand for wafer-fabrication equipment. Growth was led by equipment for advanced logic and memory, while a strong first-quarter outlook and management's projection for a rapidly expanding equipment market point to continued investment. Supply-chain and fab capacity will determine how quickly that demand becomes shipments.

title: Asus expects the 2027 PC market to shrink 10–15% as memory costs bite
snippet: Asus has turned cautious on the 2027 PC market, forecasting a 10–15% full-year decline as memory prices surge, end-user demand cools, and global regulation of data-center construction tightens. The company expects the decline to be steeper in the first half, with a gradual recovery only in the second half.

title: Asus reports record third-quarter revenue as server business grows
snippet: Asus posted record brand consolidated revenue of NT$258.788 billion (US$7.86 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, up 7% quarter-on-quarter and 36% year-on-year, as AI server shipments continued to grow. Net income rose 14% sequentially and 105% year-on-year to NT$21.631 billion.

title: Lutnick's clash with Treasury over Nvidia chip curbs deepens as White House weighs his future
snippet: A dispute between Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent over how hard to police Nvidia chip shipments to China has moved to the center of Washington's fallout from espionage allegations involving Nvidia's former CEO, with White House officials discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out and lawmakers pressing his department to add Chinese firms that have been left alone to its Entity List.

title: Remote access emerges as biggest gap in US chip controls as Congress and Commerce move to close it
snippet: The loophole that lets Chinese AI developers rent Nvidia chips in overseas data centers is becoming the main target of a tougher US export-control push. Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterms, and the Commerce Department is moving to finalize its own remote-access rule. The stakes are large: remote access accounts for about half of the US-made AI compute that Washington could still cut off from China by the end of 2027, according to the Institute for Progress (IFP).

title: LG Chem reportedly developing MR-MUF materials for HBM on top of NCF work
snippet: LG Chem is developing materials for the mass reflow-molded underfill (MR-MUF) process used to make high-bandwidth memory (HBM), Korean media outlet ETNews reported, citing industry sources. If successful, the effort would widen the range of critical HBM materials produced in South Korea and reduce reliance on imports.

title: Last night, Apple briefly removed Telegram from the App Store because a single user had planted illegal pornographic content in a public gro
snippet:
Last night, Apple briefly removed Telegram from the App Store because a single user had planted illegal pornographic content in a public group chat.

⬅️ Telegram was restored within hours. But I want to explain what happened — to warn other app developers and help protect online communities from similar attacks.

🧹Because Telegram quickly removes illegal content from public groups using all kinds of moderation tools, the attacker had to resort to a technical trick. He inserted AI-modified illegal content by editing an old message in an active group chat. As a result, the content was effectively hidden from the group’s members, preventing them from seeing and promptly reporting it.

title: A high-school student just made $20,000 from a Telegram Gift.
snippet:
A high-school student just made $20,000 from a Telegram Gift.

Jonathan He, an IOI gold medalist ranked #7 in the world, sold his Algorithm Cup — an NFT we gave to the top young coders this month — for 💎 15,000 Grams.

Happy for him. It's a meaningful sum for someone still in school, and I suspect a small fraction of what he'll go on to build.

20 years ago, $20K was enough for me to launch my first company. Within months, it had reached 1M users and raised $12M at a $60M valuation. 💸

I hope some of this year's winners put their Grams to similar use! 📈
